diagnosis_explanation: Your voice box is irritated. This is called chronic laryngitis. It can make your voice sound rough or weak. This is called hoarseness.
medication_rationale: Your doctor did not give you any new medicines to take at home. Ask at your next visit if you need to start any.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will likely feel tired and hoarse.
- Rest your voice as much as possible.
- Speak only when absolutely necessary.
- Avoid talking or making noise.
- Drink plenty of water.
- Your goal is to rest your voice completely.
- Call your doctor if your voice gets worse.

**Week 2:**
- You may start to feel less tired.
- Speak in a soft, gentle voice.
- Avoid loud talking or shouting.
- Do not whisper, this can strain your voice.
- Continue drinking lots of water.
- Your goal is to use your voice softly.
- Call your doctor if you have pain when you speak.

**Week 3:**
- Your voice may feel stronger.
- Practice gentle resonant voice exercises daily.
- Focus on breathing and relaxed speech.
- Avoid clearing your throat forcefully.
- Continue vocal hygiene practices.
- Your goal is to do your exercises for 10 minutes.
- Call your doctor if hoarseness returns strongly.

**Week 4:**
- You should feel more comfortable using your voice.
- Gradually increase talking time each day.
- Use your resonant voice techniques in conversation.
- Avoid smoky or dusty environments.
- Continue relaxation and stretching exercises.
- Your goal is to talk for 15 minutes at a time.
- Call your doctor if you experience significant discomfort.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Your voice should continue to improve over the next few weeks.
- Keep practicing your voice exercises daily.
- Maintain good vocal hygiene habits.
- Listen to your body and rest your voice when needed.
- Progress may be slow, but it is steady.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- No symptoms in this tier for your diagnosis.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- No symptoms in this tier for your diagnosis.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Hoarseness lasting over 2 weeks: Your voice box may be sore.
- Trouble breathing or swallowing: This could block your airway.
- Coughing up blood: This can be a serious sign.
- Sudden voice loss: Your vocal cords may be hurt.
- Severe throat pain: This can mean a bad infection.
